about: Custom parts (DESIGN 5.19 and 6.5), as the runtimes of the web stacks (Rust, Go, C, C++) carry them; on Avalonia the view model holds them as typed properties. A custom part's properties are part state held by name, as the renderer sends them back with each event: `read` gives what reading one gives (null when the state has none, and the generated code then takes the value written in the window or the declared default), `set` what setting one leaves in the part's state. A hear (`arena.restart(2)`) goes out with the reply, in the order the handler gave them: `hear` gives the hears given and the reply's `hears`, left out when there are none.
